root_cause.text: In EROFS file-backed readahead, `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()` treated a short `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` result as a successful read and still completed the whole bio as uptodate, so a signal-interrupted partial read left unused folios incorrectly marked valid.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message say `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` can be interrupted by `SIGKILL` and return only the bytes actually copied, yet `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()` would “set all folios uptodate”; the patch fixes this by changing `if (ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size)` from zero-filling the remainder to `ret = -EIO`, preventing short reads from being completed as success.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE and commit message say `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` can be interrupted by `SIGKILL` and return only the bytes actually copied, yet `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()` would “set all folios uptodate”; the patch fixes this by changing `if (ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size)` from zero-filling the remainder to `ret = -EIO`, preventing short reads from being completed as success.

intent_record.intent_summary: Treat short file I/O completions as errors instead of zero-filling the remainder.
intent_record.what: In `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()`, the partial-read handling block was changed from advancing the bio and zero-filling the remaining portion when `ret` was non-negative but shorter than `rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size`, to instead setting `ret = -EIO` in that case. The surrounding control flow and the later `if (!rq->bio.bi_end_io)` block were left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, a short successful I/O completion is no longer treated as a recoverable partial transfer with the remainder zero-filled; instead it is converted into an I/O error. This prevents the code from silently accepting incomplete reads and forces the caller/error path to handle the failure explicitly.

grouping_result.intent: Treat short file I/O completions as errors instead of zero-filling the remainder.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes handling of short file I/O completions so they are not treated as successful full reads, which is what caused partially read folios to be incorrectly marked uptodate.

candidates.rationale: This conditional treats any non-negative short read as a normal completion path rather than an error, which is the root cause of marking the whole bio uptodate after a signal-interrupted partial read.
This line shows the vulnerable behavior of zero-filling the remainder after a short read, which allowed unused folios to be considered valid instead of failing the I/O.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition treats any non-negative short read as a normal completion path, which allows a signal-interrupted partial read to proceed as if it succeeded and leads to the whole bio being marked uptodate.
This statement zero-fills the remainder after a short read, masking the partial completion and causing unused folios to be treated as valid instead of propagating an I/O failure.

diff --git a/fs/erofs/fileio.c b/f
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the completion path in `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()`. The vulnerable construct from the root cause is the handling of short reads: the old code only treated `ret > 0` as the partial-read case, then advanced and zero-filled, and crucially did not distinguish a short read from a full successful read when completing folios. The fix is present in the new code: `if (ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size) { bio_advance(&rq->bio, ret); zero_fill_bio(&rq->bio); }` and, more importantly, `erofs_onlinefolio_end(fi.folio, ret < 0, false);` now marks folios failed only on error, not on short-but-successful reads. This directly addresses the root cause where a signal-interrupted partial read could leave unused folios marked uptodate.
